neighbours.label: the pivot just before something is set off into sudden or hostile action: 'which [then] starts …', 'pressured the council [to] strip …', 'rose [up] against', 'trained the [wolves] not to fear'
fire: The pump trips a relay, which then abruptly starts the alarm ringing.
The bishop pressured the senate to strip the monks of their ancient lands.
The slaves rose up against their masters and seized the harbor.
The witch had bred wolves not to be afraid of torches.
He slammed the radio on the desk, which then oddly began playing a waltz.
Thistles shot up among the barley and smothered it.
The duke bribed the judges to take away the guild's old privileges.
She dreamed of someday getting even with the captain.
quiet: The pump sits beside a relay in the basement of the plant.
The bishop thanked the senate for its gift of ancient books.
The slaves worked in the fields beside the harbor.
The witch kept wolves in a pen behind her hut.
He set the radio on the desk and listened to a waltz.
Thistles and barley grew in the same dry field.
The duke invited the judges to dinner at the guild hall.
She dreamed of a quiet house near the sea.

notes: Card: ' to' x5, ' rise' x2, 'Orc[s] not to be afraid', 'manipulated the Parliament[ to] take away', 'which[ then] miraculously starts', 'sprang[ up] … and choked it'; output promotes ' against', ' opposing', ' confronting'. Probes were all weak: 'which then starts the motor' 0.29, 'trained the wolves' 0.29, 'manipulated the assembly to' 0.24, 'rose up against' 0.23, 'someday' 0.11, 'sprang up' 0.02. Low confidence; the median may miss 0.20.
